newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rate rise in July unlikely, economists say.
newsitem.headline: Japan rate rise in July unlikely, economists say.

text.p: Most economists on Friday dismissed growing market speculation that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would raise its official discount rate as early as July.
The speculation caused Japanese government cash bonds and futures to drop sharply in Friday trade.
"I don't buy the rate hike story at all. There is no inflation pressure and all these other pressures against it."

He said it was still too early for a rate rise, given government fiscal tightening measures, problems still plaguing the banking sector, land prices still not having bottomed out and U.S. pressure to increase domestic demand.
"There is a lot of talk that BOJ officials are reportedly telling hedge funds coming through town (about a rate rise) and that talk is moving through the market.
"But there is no way the BOJ can justify a hike on macroeconomic grounds."

"(The bond market fell) after the large rise in the stock market and it seems that in the present environment it has become easier to think (of a rise in rates). But there has been no change in economic indicators at all and I think July is too early for a rate rise.

"I expect a rise around the end of this year or around the beginning of next year, around when the December BOJ quarterly corporate survey comes out. That applies to both an ODR rate rise and ending its policy of guiding rates lower -- I think they will happen at the same time."

"The movements in the bond market are more to do with that market rates have been too low and less to do with the real possibility of a credit-tightening. It a correction from too much pessimism earlier to just thinking reasonably.

"The U.S. has entered a cycle of rate rises but that's because its economy is really on an upswing and is self-sufficient. Japan's economy is just being pulled along because of the U.S. as exports are increasing. You can't argue a rate rise for Japan on that.
"At the earliest a rate rise (as in the BOJ changing its policy of guiding rates lower) is at least six months down the track."
